content:
Unless I'm missing something, docs#Equiv.constSMul is a duplicate of docs#MulAction.toPerm with uselessly strong assumptions (docs#Torsor instead of docs#MulAction).

I was going to suggest simply nuking Equiv.constSMul in favor of MulAction.toPerm (which is probably pre-existing ? I didn't check), but I realize the reason the duplication was added is probably that the name constSMul is more discoverable. Any thoughts?
Note an extra complication: docs#Equiv.constVAddHom is Multiplicative G →* Perm P, while docs#AddAction.toPermHom is G →+ Additive (Perm α)...
MulAction.toPerm always struck me as an odd name. I would be happy to nuke that name instead (along with its DistribMulAction variant, etc)
There are a very large number of variants that use the MulAction.toPerm naming

Anatole Dedecker said:

with uselessly strong assumptions (docs#Torsor instead of docs#MulAction).

Isn't torsor mathematically more general?
it's not. Torsor G P extends MulAction G P by assuming that P is nonempty and that there is an inverse operation sdiv : P -> P -> G which is lawful in various ways.
Perhaps what I mean then is "are we sure that either is more general than the other"?
Yes, MulAction is strictly more general, both mathematically and in Mathlib.
Ah apologies, I did not realize that Torsor required G to be a group
Equiv.constSMul would I think be a better general name.
